overall_diagnosis: All samples converge on a single gap in maven-build-lifecycle/SKILL.md: the Maven CI repair workflow does not adequately explain how dependency resolution works for nested integration-test/fixture projects (e.g., Maven Invoker-style projects under src/it or similar) and gives insufficient guidance on where fixes should be applied (parent reactor vs nested project POMs vs settings/local repo). This can lead to editing the wrong POM/module or making overly broad dependency changes that don’t affect the actual failing nested build context.

diagnosed_skills.diagnosis: Missing/unclear workflow guidance for diagnosing and fixing dependency resolution failures that occur inside nested test projects (Invoker/IT fixtures) rather than the main reactor. Also lacks clear rules for the permissible modification scope, causing users to patch parent POMs when the failure is isolated to a nested fixture, or to over-modify unrelated modules.
diagnosed_skills.repair_instruction: Revise the CI reproduction and repair workflow to explicitly cover nested test projects/fixtures: (1) how to identify when a failure originates from an embedded/nested Maven project (locations like src/it/**, invoker projects, sample apps) vs the main reactor; (2) how to reproduce and inspect those failures (run the phase that executes them, check invoker reports/logs, use -e/-X, verify local repo state); (3) explain dependency resolution boundaries (nested project POM coordinates and inheritance—when it inherits parent dependencyManagement/pluginManagement vs when it is intentionally standalone); (4) add a decision rule for where to apply fixes: prefer minimal changes, apply to parent management only when the nested project inherits it, otherwise patch only the nested fixture POM/config; (5) add explicit modification-scope constraints to avoid broad refactors/modernization when only the nested test project is broken.
